# Verdict: REJECT **Overall Assessment**: `BuggyCombobox` implements the surface appearance of a combobox but completely omits the assistive technology communication layer required by the WAI-ARIA 1.2 Combobox pattern. While keyboard event handlers exist for arrow navigation and Enter/Escape, the suggestions container and options have no ARIA roles, no `aria-activedescendant` wiring, and no `aria-controls` reference—rendering the entire suggestions list completely invisible, unnavigable, and inaudible to screen reader users. **Pre-commitment Predictions**: - *Prediction*: Missing `role="listbox"` on popup container, missing `role="option"` and `aria-selected` on items. - *Prediction*: DOM focus stays in ``, but `aria-activedescendant` is not wired up, causing screen readers to remain silent on Arrow key presses. - *Prediction*: Missing `aria-controls` pairing between `` and the popup container. - *Actual*: All predicted issues were confirmed directly in the source code; in addition, selection state is communicated solely through visual CSS classes (`.selected`), and edge cases in arrow navigation risk runtime state corruption. --- ## Findings ### Critical Findings (Blocks Access) 1. **Popup suggestions container missing `role="listbox"`** - **Location**: `BuggyCombobox.jsx:68-71` - **Element**: `
` - **Impacted Group**: Screen reader users - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WAI-ARIA APG Combobox Pattern; WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value; WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Why this matters**: The container `#suggestions-popup` renders as a generic unsemantic `
`. Screen readers cannot identify it as the popup list associated with the combobox. - **Fix**: Add `role="listbox"` and `aria-label={label}` (or `aria-labelledby="combobox-input"`) to the popup container: ```jsx
``` 2. **Suggestions items missing `role="option"`, unique IDs, and `aria-selected`** - **Location**: `BuggyCombobox.jsx:72-80` - **Element**: `
` - **Impacted Group**: Screen reader users - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WAI-ARIA APG Combobox Pattern; WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Why this matters**: Items inside the list are unsemantic `
` elements. They lack `role="option"` and communicate selection exclusively via the visual CSS class `.selected`. Assistive technology users receive zero indication of item role, list position (e.g., "1 of 5"), or selection state. - **Fix**: Assign `role="option"`, a deterministic `id`, and programmatic selection state: ```jsx {filtered.map((option, idx) => (
handleSelect(option)} onMouseDown={(e) => e.preventDefault()} className={selectedIndex === idx ? 'suggestion-item selected' : 'suggestion-item'} > {option}
))} ``` 3. **Missing `aria-activedescendant` on combobox `` during arrow navigation** - **Location**: `BuggyCombobox.jsx:55-65` - **Element**: `` - **Impacted Group**: Screen reader users, keyboard-only screen reader users - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WAI-ARIA APG Combobox Pattern (Active Descendant); WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value; WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Why this matters**: In a combobox with a listbox popup, DOM focus remains inside the `` element while the user presses ArrowDown and ArrowUp. Because `aria-activedescendant` is never set, the screen reader does not announce the highlighted suggestion as the user steps through items. To a blind user, pressing arrow keys produces total silence. - **Fix**: Bind `aria-activedescendant` to the highlighted item's ID when active: ```jsx aria-activedescendant={ isOpen && selectedIndex >= 0 ? `combobox-option-${selectedIndex}` : undefined } ``` --- ### Major Findings (Significantly Degrades Experience) 1. **Combobox input lacks `aria-controls` pointing to suggestions popup** - **Location**: `BuggyCombobox.jsx:55-65` - **Element**: `` - **Impacted Group**: Screen reader users - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WAI-ARIA APG Combobox Pattern (ARIA 1.2); WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Why this matters**: Under the ARIA 1.2 Combobox specification, `role="combobox"` requires an `aria-controls` attribute referencing the `id` of the element controlled by the combobox (`suggestions-popup`). Without this, assistive technology cannot establish the parent-popup programmatic relationship. - **Fix**: Add `aria-controls="suggestions-popup"` to the ``. 2. **Missing `aria-haspopup="listbox"` on combobox ``** - **Location**: `BuggyCombobox.jsx:55-65` - **Element**: `` - **Impacted Group**: Screen reader users - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WAI-ARIA APG Combobox Pattern; WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Why this matters**: Although ARIA 1.2 defines `listbox` as the default popup type for comboboxes, legacy screen readers and multiple browser engines still rely on explicit `aria-haspopup="listbox"` to announce that activating the combobox will spawn a list of choices. - **Fix**: Add `aria-haspopup="listbox"` to the `` attributes. 3. **Potential index corruption and state error when filtering yields zero results** - **Location**: `BuggyCombobox.jsx:32-35, 42-44` - **Code**: `const nextIdx = selectedIndex < filtered.length - 1 ? selectedIndex + 1 : 0;` and `handleSelect(filtered[selectedIndex])` - **Impacted Group**: Keyboard-only users, cognitive accessibility users - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard; WCAG 3.3.4 Error Prevention - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Why this matters**: If `filtered.length === 0` and the user presses keys while `isOpen` is toggled or when manipulating state, `nextIdx` resolves to `0`. If Enter is triggered, `filtered[0]` is `undefined`, passing `undefined` to `handleSelect(undefined)` and `setInput(undefined)`. In React, passing `undefined` to a controlled input value switches it to uncontrolled, causing console errors and unpredictable UI behavior. - **Fix**: Guard arrow navigation and selection with `filtered.length > 0`: ```jsx if (filtered.length === 0) return; ``` --- ### Minor Findings (Friction / Edge Cases) 1. **Option selection lacks `onMouseDown` preventDefault** - **Location**: `BuggyCombobox.jsx:75` - **Impacted Group**: Mouse & touch users, screen magnifier users - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard / Focus Management - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Why this matters**: Clicking an option triggers a mouse focus shift from the ``, which can disrupt focus management or preemptively fire blur events if blur-to-dismiss behavior is added later. - **Fix**: Add `onMouseDown={(e) => e.preventDefault()}` on each option element so focus remains on the `` during click selection. 2. **Incomplete state reset on Escape key press** - **Location**: `BuggyCombobox.jsx:45-48` - **Impacted Group**: Keyboard users, screen reader users - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard - **Confidence**: MEDIUM - **Why this matters**: Pressing Escape sets `setIsOpen(false)` but preserves `selectedIndex`. Reopening the menu can resume with an outdated index selected. - **Fix**: Reset `setSelectedIndex(-1)` on Escape. --- ### Enhancements (Best Practice) 1. **Missing dynamic status announcements for filtered result counts** - **WCAG Citation**: WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages - **Suggestion**: Add a visually hidden `aria-live="polite"` status element (e.g., announcing "3 suggestions available" or "No suggestions found") so screen reader users know whether typing yielded any valid options. --- ### What's Missing (Gaps & Unhandled Edge Cases) - **Missing programmatic state synchronization**: The selection state is strictly visual via `.selected` CSS class; there is no `aria-selected` attribute on items. - **Missing active descendant tracking**: No `aria-activedescendant` mechanism exists to bridge keyboard navigation in the input to the virtual selection in the list. - **Missing popup container semantics**: No `role="listbox"` on the popup and no `role="option"` on child nodes. - **Missing element linkage**: No `aria-controls="suggestions-popup"` on the input element. - **Missing empty-state feedback**: No feedback or live region messaging when a filter produces zero results. --- ## Perspective Alarm Levels | Perspective | Alarm Level | Trigger Signal | |---|---|---| | Screen reader | **HIGH** | Complete absence of `role="listbox"`, `role="option"`, `aria-activedescendant`, `aria-selected`, and `aria-controls`. | | Keyboard-only | **MEDIUM** | Key handlers exist but lack boundary guards for empty lists and have incomplete Escape reset logic. | | Low vision | **MEDIUM** | Requires verification of focus indicator and contrast on the `.selected` state (≥ 3:1 component boundary, ≥ 4.5:1 text). | | Cognitive | **MEDIUM** | Unannounced visual list updates and potential React state corruption if `undefined` is selected. | | Vestibular & motion | **LOW** | No motion, animations, or transitions present. | | Auditory access | **LOW** | No multimedia or audio signals present. | | Environmental contrast | **MEDIUM** | `.selected` styling must maintain contrast in high-contrast/forced-colors modes. | --- ## Multi-Perspective Notes - **Screen reader user (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver)**: Focusing the input announces a combobox with autocomplete list. However, when typing and pressing arrow keys, the screen reader does not announce any options, cannot perceive the popup container, and provides no indication that an option is highlighted. The autocomplete interaction is unusable via screen reader. - **Keyboard-only user**: Arrow keys navigate the list and Enter selects, but if no suggestions match, navigation can attempt to access invalid indices. Escape closes the popup but fails to reset the active selection index. - **Low vision user**: Requires strong contrast between the `.selected` background, default background, and text. Visual focus remains in the text box, so clear visual differentiation for the highlighted option is critical. - **Cognitive accessibility**: Predictable input handling is compromised if pressing Enter on an empty query sets `undefined` into the text box. --- ## Summary `BuggyCombobox` is rejected due to **3 Critical** and **3 Major** accessibility design failures. While it includes basic ARIA scaffolding (`role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-autocomplete`), it misses the essential 20% that makes the interaction model functional for assistive technology: `role="listbox"`, `role="option"`, `aria-selected`, `aria-activedescendant`, and `aria-controls`. ### Required Remediations to Upgrade to ACCEPT: 1. Add `role="listbox"` and accessible naming to `#suggestions-popup`. 2. Add `role="option"`, deterministic `id`s (`combobox-option-${idx}`), and `aria-selected={selectedIndex === idx}` to all rendered options. 3. Add `aria-controls="suggestions-popup"` and `aria-haspopup="listbox"` to the ``. 4. Implement `aria-activedescendant={isOpen && selectedIndex >= 0 ? `combobox-option-${selectedIndex}` : undefined}` on ``. 5. Guard arrow navigation against empty filtered options to prevent state corruption. --- ## Open Questions (Unscored) 1. *Selection behavior*: Should keyboard arrow navigation auto-fill the input value as the user steps through items, or should it only highlight suggestions until Enter is pressed? (Currently it only highlights). 2. *Blur behavior*: Is this combobox intended to close when the input loses focus (`onBlur`)? If so, ensuring `onMouseDown={(e) => e.preventDefault()}` on options is strictly required to prevent focus loss before item selection.
